binh_thuy: Bình Thủy Môn, ferrymen of a sea strait: clean, well-cut tunics and wide trousers of undyed sailcloth, salt-white and pressed, tied at the waist with a cord of dried duckweed (green-brown, knotted); captains add a glossy dark-amber oilskin coat; rope-soled shoes or bare feet; a small pale shell on a string at the neck; sea wind in the cloth.
van_khoi: Vân Khởi Tự, an abbey of sitters on a bare mountain: plain grey hemp robes of good close weave, clean and neatly mended, with a visible square patch at each knee from sitting on rock; a rope belt; bare or straw-sandalled feet; the head wears nothing more, and the Reader alone carries a small bronze hand bell.
cung_tinh: Củng Tinh Quán, star-watchers of a high plain: robes of yellow-brown cloth the colour of dry grass, well kept, cross-collared, with a plain sash; a hairpin of dark star-iron (a short grey-black rod) through the topknot; straw sandals; no ornament otherwise; a cloudless sky in every light.
thai_chi: Thải Chi Cốc, herb-pickers of a terraced valley: knee-length field aprons of stiff cream cloth over undyed linen shirts and trousers, clean and well made, wide straw hats, bare feet; sleeves rolled to the elbow; a small cloth satchel of herbs; green stains at the fingertips as the only colour.
hong_dau: Hồng Đậu Trang, a manor of red-bean gardens: at the door, silk in red and rose, fitted and fine, with a single bright red bean on a thin red string at the throat; in the garden, clean grey cotton and a wide conical banana-leaf hat; the mistress wears full red; no other jewellery.
hoa_tinh: Họa Tinh Đường, talisman painters of a mountain hall: black robes of close matte cloth that hide soot, cross-collared with narrow sleeves; a black cord tied at the left wrist; hair bound up with a slim bamboo brush stuck through the knot; ink-dark fingertips; no bright colour except the faint violet of the hall's fungus dye at a hem or cuff.
